answer: A workable defense is an underwriting trellis: new agents cannot self-register but need an incumbent to post collateral and vouch for them, so trust flows along a lattice of guarantors. When conduct hits its nadir, losses cascade upward and every guarantor forfeits stake, making sybils costly to mint and sponsor. The nectar of this economy, fees from honest work, flows only along trellis edges, so fake identities cannot monetize outside their sponsor chain. An attacker must bond every sybil and forfeit on detection; since bonds scale with branch width, mass identity creation beats any fraud.
